template:
You are a senior software delivery consultant who estimates custom software projects for a development agency. Your estimates are used to quote and plan real projects, so they must be realistic, detailed and internally consistent.

Below are historical estimates from past projects. Each one shows a meeting summary and the estimation that was produced from it. Use them to learn the structure, the level of task detail, the way hours are scaled to project size and complexity, and the way contingency is applied. Do not copy their tasks, hours or technologies: every project is different, and your estimate must follow the project you are given.
---
{examples}
---

Now estimate the project described in the user's meeting summary or transcription. Work as follows:
1. Read the whole input first. Identify the goal, the scope that is included, what is explicitly excluded, the constraints (budget, deadline, regulation, team or client availability, scale), the technology stack, the integrations, and the agreed assumptions.
2. Group the work into phases that fit this project. Use only the phases the project needs, and do not copy the phase list of the examples if it does not fit.
3. Break each phase into concrete tasks, each describing what is built and, when useful, the technology or quantity involved. Keep tasks small enough to be estimated with confidence, and make sure every included feature has tasks that cover it.
4. Include the work that is easy to forget: setup, CI/CD and environments, observability, testing and QA, security, data migration, documentation, training, release and support after launch, and project management and client coordination, in the proportion the project needs.
5. Do not add work that is out of scope, and do not invent requirements. Where the input leaves a detail open, use the most common approach for the stated stack and constraints.
6. Size each task in hours, as the effort of the people doing the work for a team of average seniority. A task has a positive number of hours, and a small project must have a small estimate: do not add phases or overhead that the project does not justify.
7. Finish with a phase named Contingency containing one task. Its name states the percentage and the main drivers, and its size reflects the risks and unknowns in the input: lower for small and well-understood work, higher for integrations, legacy systems, hardware or experimental work.
8. Recommend the team (role, number of people, and whether the role is part-time) and a duration range in weeks. The team must be able to deliver the total hours inside the duration, taking into account the constraints and any stated deadline.

Return only a JSON object with the fields "phases" (each with a name and a list of tasks with name and hours), "team" (role, count, part_time) and "duration" (min_weeks, max_weeks). Do not include totals, prices or any other text: totals are computed from the phases.

meeting.title: Discovery call — Inventory & Purchasing Platform for Norte Distribuciones

meeting_summary.context_and_problem: Norte Distribuciones is a mid-size distributor of industrial spare parts (about 12,000 active SKUs, 3 warehouses in two cities, 45 employees, about 600 orders/day). Inventory is tracked today in shared Excel files plus a 12-year-old desktop ERP (SAP Business One 9.3, on-premise) that is only used for invoicing. Consequences reported by the client: frequent stock-outs of fast-moving parts, about 4% mismatch between physical and recorded stock, purchase orders created by email, and no visibility of stock across warehouses. Stock counts take 2 full days per quarter.
meeting_summary.goal: Replace the spreadsheets with a web-based inventory and purchasing platform that gives real-time stock per warehouse, tracks every stock movement, automates reorder suggestions, and manages purchase orders end to end. Success criteria stated by the client: stock accuracy above 98%, stock-outs of top-200 SKUs reduced by 50% within 6 months, quarterly count reduced to 1 day.
in_scope: Product catalog: SKUs with variants, categories, units of measure, supplier(s), min/max stock levels. Bulk CSV import/export.
Multi-warehouse and bin-location management (3 warehouses, about 40 locations each).
Stock movements ledger: goods receipt, issue, transfer between warehouses, manual adjustment with reason. Every movement is immutable and audited.
Purchase orders: supplier management, PO creation, approval flow (2 levels above a configurable amount), partial receipts, PDF/email to supplier.
Low-stock alerts and reorder suggestions based on min levels and last-90-day consumption.
Barcode support: generate labels (Code128) and scan with the phone camera from the browser (no native app).
Dashboard: stock value, stock-outs, slow movers, open POs, movements per day. Reports exportable to CSV/XLSX.
Roles: Admin, Warehouse Operator, Purchasing, Read-only (manager). Login with the client's Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC SSO).
One-way sync of products and stock levels to the existing SAP B1, running hourly (confirmed in the call).
One-time migration of current Excel data.
UI in Spanish and English.
out_of_scope: Sales orders / e-commerce
Invoicing
Native mobile apps
Offline mode
Demand forecasting with ML
RFID
Multi-currency accounting
Supplier portal
Lot/serial/expiry tracking (confirmed not needed)
Hardware procurement: scanners and label printers (the client buys them)
constraints: Budget ceiling communicated informally: about USD 55k.
Hard deadline: go-live before the high season starting 2026-09-01, so development must finish by mid-July at the latest. Kickoff is planned for 2026-04-06.
Data residency: data must stay in the AWS sa-east-1 (Sao Paulo) region.
The IT Coordinator is only available about 4 h/week; business stakeholders can attend one weekly 1-hour demo/feedback session.
Warehouse Wi-Fi is unreliable in one location; the UI must tolerate slow connections (no offline mode, but retries and clear error states).
Users are not technical: the main flows (receive, issue, transfer) must take at most 3 taps/clicks from the home screen on a phone.
Target scale: up to 15 concurrent users, 12k SKUs, about 2,000 movements/day, 5 years of history.

proposed_stack.frontend: React 18 + TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Query, Tailwind + component library, PWA for camera scanning (ZXing).
proposed_stack.backend: Node.js 20 + NestJS (REST, OpenAPI), PostgreSQL 15 (RDS), Prisma ORM, BullMQ + Redis for background jobs (imports, alerts, ERP sync).
proposed_stack.auth: Microsoft Entra ID via OIDC, roles mapped from groups.
proposed_stack.infra: AWS (ECS Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SES, CloudWatch), Terraform, GitHub Actions CI/CD, 3 environments (dev, staging, prod).
proposed_stack.quality: Jest, React Testing Library, Playwright, Sentry.

integrations: Microsoft Entra ID (SSO): client IT already has a tenant and will create the app registration.

SAP Business One 9.3 on-premise: the Service Layer is enabled (confirmed by client IT during the call). Access from AWS goes through a site-to-site VPN that client IT will provide; sync is one-way (platform to SAP) and hourly.
Amazon SES for email; supplier email templates provided by the client.
assumptions: Client provides Excel data within 2 weeks of kickoff; data cleaning of up to 12k rows is done by the client, we only validate and load it.
A single approval workflow (configurable threshold), not a generic workflow engine.
Up to 18 distinct screens in the high-fidelity design; the client has no brand guide beyond a logo.
Client feedback within 2 business days; one consolidated round of changes per demo.
2 UAT cycles of 1 week each, executed by the client.
Purchase order approval: orders up to USD 2,000 are approved by the Purchasing Manager; above that, the COO also approves. The threshold is configurable by an Admin.
Reports beyond the dashboard: 5 reports (stock by warehouse, movements by period, slow movers, supplier performance, open POs).
The client provides the label printer (Zebra, 100x50 mm labels) and the scanners; Bluetooth/USB HID scanners work as keyboard input with no extra development.
Spanish/English scope includes the UI, emails and PDFs.
Support after hypercare is out of this estimate and handled under a separate agreement.

risks.description: SAP B1 9.3 is an old version; the Service Layer is enabled but the integration depends on the client's VPN and on SAP-side permissions being granted on time.
Data quality of the Excel files (duplicate SKUs, inconsistent units) may delay migration and the stock accuracy goal.
Limited client availability (IT 4 h/week) can block SSO setup, VPN and UAT.
Budget (about 55k) is tight relative to scope; scope creep around reports and approval rules is likely.
Browser camera barcode scanning is less reliable on low-end Android devices and in low light; the fallback is a USB/Bluetooth HID scanner.
Fixed go-live date before high season leaves little slack; any delay in kickoff impacts directly.

meeting.title: Discovery call — Internal Knowledge Assistant (RAG) for Ingenia Consultores

meeting_summary.context_and_problem: Ingenia is a 300-person engineering consultancy with 15 years of project reports, technical standards, proposals and internal policies spread over SharePoint Online (about 85,000 documents), Confluence Cloud (about 9,000 pages) and file shares that were already migrated to SharePoint libraries (about 26,000 documents). In total there are about 120,000 documents, mostly PDF and Word, and roughly 15% (about 18,000) are scanned PDFs without a text layer. Engineers report spending 3 to 5 hours per week looking for precedent (previous designs, calculation memos, standard clauses), and a survey of 80 engineers showed that 60% give up and rebuild from scratch at least once a month. Search in SharePoint is keyword-only, ignores scanned files and does not work across Confluence. Content is bilingual: about 70% Spanish and 30% English.
meeting_summary.goal: Build an internal assistant that answers engineering questions in Spanish and English with citations to the source documents, available inside Microsoft Teams. Success criteria stated by the client: at least 85% of answers on a curated set of 150 questions rated correct and grounded by two senior engineers, at least 90% of answers carry a valid citation, no user ever sees a document they cannot open in the source system, p95 latency of the first token under 6 seconds, and an average LLM plus search cost below USD 0.08 per question. A pilot with 40 engineers runs for 3 weeks after go-live.
in_scope: Ingestion of about 120,000 documents (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX text, Confluence pages) from SharePoint Online via Microsoft Graph API and from Confluence Cloud via the REST API, with an initial full load and incremental sync every 2 hours (Celery workers with Redis).
OCR with Amazon Textract for the about 18,000 scanned PDFs, with a quality check on a sample of 200 pages and a fallback path for failed pages.
Document parsing and structure-aware chunking (headings, tables, page numbers kept as metadata), with 3 chunking strategies compared in a time-boxed experiment and one selected.
Embeddings with Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 and storage in an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection that holds vectors, BM25 fields and ACL metadata.
Hybrid retrieval (vector plus BM25, fused), reranking with Cohere Rerank on Amazon Bedrock, query rewriting for follow-up questions and language detection (ES/EN, cross-language retrieval).
Answer generation with Anthropic Claude on Amazon Bedrock, orchestrated with LlamaIndex, with inline citations (document title, page, link to the source), and a clear 'no answer found' behavior.

Permission-aware search: the ACLs (SharePoint groups and users, Confluence space and page restrictions) are synced into document-level security filters in OpenSearch, evaluated per user identity from Microsoft Entra ID, with a permission sync every 30 minutes.

Microsoft Teams bot (Bot Framework SDK) for personal chat, with streaming-style progressive replies, Adaptive Cards for citations, thumbs up/down feedback with an optional comment, and Entra ID single sign-on.

Guardrails: prompt-injection and jailbreak filtering on documents and questions, off-topic handling, PII masking in logs, hallucination control by grounding checks and citation verification, rate limits of 30 questions per user per hour.
Prompt versioning (prompts stored in the repository and released with a version tag), Langfuse tracing of every request and token cost monitoring per user group, with a budget alarm.

Evaluation harness: a curated set of 150 questions (100 Spanish, 50 English) with reference answers and source documents, Ragas metrics (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision and recall) run in CI and on demand, plus a human review round of 2 days by two senior engineers.
Feedback capture stored in an OpenSearch index and a weekly feedback report as a CSV exported to the Knowledge Management team.

Infrastructure as code with Terraform on AWS (ECS Fargate, ElastiCache Redis, OpenSearch Serverless, Bedrock access, S3, Secrets Manager), GitHub Actions CI/CD, 2 environments (staging and production).
Documentation, a 1-hour training session for the pilot group, a 1-page user guide and 2 weeks of hypercare after go-live.
out_of_scope: A standalone web chat interface (Teams is the only channel)
Fine-tuning or training of any model
Answers generated from images, drawings, CAD files or the content of embedded images (only text and OCR text are indexed)
Voice interface and Microsoft Teams channel or group-chat bots
Ingestion of email, Slack or ERP data
Document authoring or summarization workflows beyond question answering
Cleanup, deduplication or reclassification of the document repositories by Ingenia content owners
Translation of the document corpus
Support and model-quality tuning after hypercare (handled under a separate agreement)
constraints: Budget ceiling communicated by the CTO: about USD 70k for the build, excluding AWS and Bedrock consumption.
Kickoff on 2026-02-02 and a pilot go-live target of mid-May 2026 (about 15 weeks), before the Q2 proposal season.
Data residency: all data and model inference must stay in AWS us-east-1 (Bedrock models available there); no document content may leave the Ingenia AWS account.
ACL fidelity is mandatory: the IT Security Officer must sign off a permission test on 50 documents with known restrictions before the pilot.
The Microsoft 365 Administrator is available about 4 hours per week and is the only person who can grant Graph API consent and Teams app approval.
The Head of Knowledge Management and two senior engineers can dedicate 3 days in total to reviewing the question set and answers.
Scale: up to 300 users, about 60 concurrent, about 1,500 questions per day at peak, and a corpus of 120,000 documents growing by about 400 per week.
Quality targets are measured on the curated set; the contract commits to the measured improvement process, not to a guaranteed percentage beyond the 85% target.

proposed_stack.backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, LlamaIndex for orchestration, Celery with Redis for ingestion and sync jobs.
proposed_stack.models: Anthropic Claude on Amazon Bedrock for answers and query rewriting, Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 for embeddings, Cohere Rerank on Amazon Bedrock.
proposed_stack.search: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (vector plus BM25 hybrid search with document-level security filters), Amazon Textract for OCR of scanned documents.
proposed_stack.connectors_and_ui: Microsoft Graph API for SharePoint, Confluence REST API, Microsoft Teams bot built with the Bot Framework SDK and Adaptive Cards.
proposed_stack.auth: Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC and Teams SSO), identities mapped to the ACL principals stored with each document.
proposed_stack.infra: AWS (ECS Fargate, ElastiCache Redis, S3, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch), Terraform, GitHub Actions CI/CD, 2 environments (staging and production).
proposed_stack.evaluation_and_ops: Ragas with a curated question set for evals, Langfuse for tracing and cost tracking, pytest for unit and integration tests.

integrations: SharePoint Online through Microsoft Graph API (application permissions Sites.Read.All and Files.Read.All): the Microsoft 365 Administrator grants admin consent and creates the app registration in the first week.
Confluence Cloud through the REST API with a read-only service account and API token that Ingenia IT provides; page restrictions are read through the same API.
Microsoft Entra ID for Teams SSO and for resolving user group memberships used by the ACL filters.
Microsoft Teams: the bot is registered in the Azure Bot Service by Ingenia IT and distributed as a custom app to the pilot group first, then to the whole tenant.
Amazon Bedrock model access (Claude, Titan Embeddings V2, Cohere Rerank) enabled in the Ingenia AWS account in us-east-1; Ingenia requests the quota increases we specify in week 1.
assumptions: The initial corpus is 120,000 documents with a median of 12 pages; documents above 300 pages (about 1,500) are indexed but truncated to the first 300 pages.
OCR covers the about 18,000 scanned PDFs, Spanish and English only; handwritten content is not indexed.
The curated question set has 150 questions, written by Ingenia engineers (we provide a template and help with 50 of them); reference answers are validated by two senior engineers.

The experimentation phase is time-boxed to 70 hours in total, with 3 chunking strategies, 2 retrieval configurations and 3 prompt iterations compared against the question set; work beyond the time-box is covered only by the contingency.
Permission sync handles users and groups from Entra ID and the native SharePoint and Confluence restrictions; sharing links created ad hoc ('anyone with the link') are treated as not accessible.
One Teams personal-chat bot, one tenant, Spanish and English UI strings; the answer language follows the language of the question.
Staging and production environments only; staging uses a 10% sample of the corpus.
Client feedback within 2 business days and one weekly 45-minute demo; the pilot of 40 users is run by Ingenia with our support.
Langfuse is self-hosted on ECS Fargate in the same account (open-source edition).
Hypercare lasts 2 weeks after the pilot go-live; support after that is out of this estimate.

risks.description: Answer quality may not reach 85% on the curated set in the planned iterations; scanned and table-heavy documents reduce retrieval accuracy, and extra tuning cycles would consume the contingency.

Document-level permissions are hard to mirror exactly (nested groups, inherited SharePoint permissions, Confluence page restrictions); a mistake would expose restricted content and block the security sign-off.
Microsoft Graph throttling and the size of the initial load (120,000 documents, 18,000 OCR jobs) may stretch the first full ingestion to several days and delay evaluation work.
Dependency on the Microsoft 365 Administrator (4 h/week) for Graph consent, Teams app approval and bot registration can delay the connector and bot work.
Bedrock quotas and latency for Claude and Cohere Rerank in us-east-1 may force throttling, caching or a smaller context, affecting the p95 latency and the cost per question targets.
Prompt injection through document content is possible in a corpus of this size; the guardrails reduce but cannot eliminate the risk.
Reviewers may disagree on what a correct answer is, which makes the evaluation set noisy and delays the quality measurement.

meeting.title: Discovery call — Multi-tenant SaaS rebuild for RutaFix

meeting_summary.context_and_problem: RutaFix is a startup that sells scheduling and dispatch software to small HVAC and plumbing companies with 5 to 80 technicians each. Three early customers (about 110 technicians in total) run on a single-tenant prototype deployed once per customer on separate Heroku apps. Each new customer needs about 3 days of manual setup, upgrades are applied three times, billing is done by hand from spreadsheets, and the prototype has no audit trail, no data export and no formal access controls. Two prospects with 60 and 80 technicians have asked for a SOC 2 report before signing, and the sales pipeline holds 25 more companies that cannot be onboarded without self-service signup.
meeting_summary.goal: Rebuild the product as a multi-tenant SaaS with self-service onboarding, automated subscription billing and the controls needed to obtain a SOC 2 Type I report. Success criteria stated by the client: a new company is live in under 30 minutes without staff involvement, 100 tenants and 2,000 technicians supported on the first production setup, billing fully automated with fewer than 1% of invoices needing manual correction, and a SOC 2 Type I report issued by the end of September 2026.
in_scope: Multi-tenancy on a shared PostgreSQL database with row-level security and acts_as_tenant, subdomain per company, and a cross-tenant isolation test suite.
Self-service onboarding wizard: signup, company profile, 14-day trial, invitations for users.
Users and 4 roles (owner, dispatcher, technician, billing admin), email and password login with TOTP two-factor, and SSO with Microsoft Entra ID and Google.
Per-tenant configuration: business hours, job types, SMS templates, branding and service areas.
Customers, sites and equipment, with CSV import.
Job scheduling and technician dispatch: job lifecycle, availability and conflict detection, dispatcher board with drag-and-drop and live updates, map view and nearest-technician suggestions.
Technician mobile web app as a PWA (8 screens): day view, job status, photos, notes, parts used, customer signature, with queued updates on weak connectivity.
Customer notifications by SMS (Twilio) and email (Postmark): confirmation, reminder and on-the-way messages, plus a self-service confirm or reschedule link.
Quotes and invoices with a price book, taxes, PDF output and per-tenant numbering.
Subscription billing with Stripe: per-technician seats, metered SMS usage, trials, proration and dunning with a read-only mode after the grace period.
Internal admin console with support impersonation limited by tenant consent and time.
Per-tenant audit log with viewer, and GDPR data export and deletion workflows.

SOC 2 Type I readiness: control mapping and evidence collection in Vanta, policies, access reviews, incident response runbook, one external penetration test and support during the auditor's Type I work.
Operations: backups and restore drills, tenant-aware observability in Datadog, per-tenant rate limiting and queue fairness, load test at 100 tenants and 2,000 technicians.
Migration of the 3 existing prototype customers into the new schema.
About 29 designed screens in total (12 dispatcher, 8 technician, 9 onboarding, billing and admin).
out_of_scope: Native iOS and Android apps
Offline-first mode with full local database on the device (only queued status updates are included)
Accepting customer payments for invoices online (invoices are marked paid manually)
Accounting integrations such as QuickBooks or Xero
Inventory and parts stock management
Public API and webhooks for customers
SOC 2 Type II observation period and report
Languages other than English
Automatic route optimization across many jobs (only nearest-technician suggestions)
Auditor and penetration test vendor fees (paid by the client)
constraints: Budget ceiling communicated by the client: about USD 260k.
Kickoff on 2026-03-02. General availability for new customers and the SOC 2 Type I report are both targeted for 2026-09-30, about 30 weeks later.

Data residency: the first production setup runs in a single Heroku Private Space in the US; EU-hosted tenants are out of the first release, so GDPR is covered by export, deletion and processing controls, not by regional hosting
The CTO is available about 6 h/week for decisions; the Head of Customer Success joins a weekly 1-hour demo.
Twilio 10DLC brand and campaign approval takes up to 4 weeks and cannot be rushed.
The auditor books Type I fieldwork 6 weeks ahead, so the control set must be operating by the middle of August.
Technicians use mid-range phones with unreliable mobile data: main job actions must work in at most 3 taps and tolerate connection loss.
Target scale at launch: 100 tenants, 2,000 technicians, about 20,000 jobs per day, 500,000 SMS per month.

proposed_stack.application: Ruby 3.3 on Rails 7.1, Hotwire (Turbo and Stimulus) for the dispatcher UI and the technician PWA, ViewComponent, Tailwind CSS.
proposed_stack.data_and_jobs: PostgreSQL 16 with row-level security and the acts_as_tenant pattern, Redis, Sidekiq for background jobs.
proposed_stack.auth: Devise with TOTP, Microsoft Entra ID and Google SSO through OmniAuth, Pundit for authorization.
proposed_stack.integrations: Stripe Billing, Twilio SMS, Mapbox maps and routing, Postmark email.
proposed_stack.infra: Heroku Private Spaces, Heroku Postgres with continuous protection, GitHub Actions, Terraform for the surrounding cloud resources (S3, KMS, IAM, DNS).
proposed_stack.quality_and_compliance: RSpec, Capybara, Brakeman, Datadog for monitoring, Vanta for SOC 2 evidence collection.

integrations: Stripe Billing: per-seat and metered prices, webhooks, customer portal. The client creates the Stripe account and provides test and live keys.

risks.description: Row-level security combined with background jobs, exports and the admin console is easy to get wrong; a single missing tenant context is a data-leak risk, so the isolation test suite must cover every entry point.

The SOC 2 Type I date depends on the auditor's calendar and on process work (policies, access reviews) that needs founder time, not only code.
Twilio 10DLC approval can take up to 4 weeks or be rejected once, which would delay SMS in production.
Migrating the 3 prototype customers means moving live operations; any data mismatch directly affects paying customers.
Dispatcher board with live updates for many dispatchers per tenant may need Turbo Streams and Redis tuning under load.
As a product company, roadmap changes during the project are likely and will compete with the fixed September date.

meeting_summary.context_and_problem: Studio Ritmo is a chain of 6 boutique fitness studios (yoga, cycling, pilates) with about 9,000 active members and around 450 classes per week. Members book through a WhatsApp group and a basic web form, and front-desk staff reconcile payments by hand. Reported pain points: about 18% of booked spots are no-shows, double bookings happen several times a week, waitlists are managed on paper, front desks spend about 25 hours per week in total reconciling class packs and monthly payments, and there is no way to remind members of their classes.

meeting.title: Discovery call - Retail Analytics Platform for Mercado Verde

meeting_summary.context_and_problem: Mercado Verde is a supermarket chain with 40 stores, about 1,800 employees and about 85,000 sales tickets per day. Sales, inventory, purchasing and loyalty data live in 9 sources: a SQL Server database in each store POS, a central Oracle ERP, a Shopify online store, the loyalty app and 5 supplier price files delivered by SFTP in different formats. Finance and category teams build their reports by hand in Excel, the monthly close takes 6 working days, and the same KPI (for example gross margin) differs by up to 3 points between departments because each team defines it differently.
meeting_summary.goal: Build a central analytics platform on Azure that ingests the 9 sources into a lakehouse, models sales, inventory, margin and loyalty with one agreed definition per metric, tests data quality, and serves 12 Power BI dashboards to four teams (finance, category and purchasing, store operations, marketing and loyalty). Success criteria stated by the client: one signed definition for each core KPI, sales reconciled with finance within 0.1%, data available by 06:00 every day, and the monthly close reporting reduced from 6 to 2 working days.
in_scope: Ingestion of the store POS SQL Servers (40 stores) with a self-hosted integration runtime, incremental loads by watermark.
Ingestion of the Oracle ERP: purchasing, inventory, item master and suppliers.
Python loaders for the Shopify API and the loyalty app REST API.
SFTP loaders for 5 supplier price file formats with schema validation and quarantine of invalid files.
Historical backfill of 24 months of POS and ERP data.
Lakehouse on Azure Databricks with PySpark and Delta Lake in bronze, silver and gold layers on ADLS Gen2, governed with Unity Catalog.
Dimensional model and metric models in dbt Core on Databricks SQL: sales, inventory, purchasing, margin and loyalty.
4 definition workshops with finance and category teams and a signed business glossary.
Data contracts per source and Great Expectations checks on 15 critical tables.
3 Power BI semantic models and 12 dashboards (3 per team), with row-level security by store region.
3 environments (dev, test, prod) with Terraform, Azure DevOps pipelines and Power BI deployment pipelines.
2 UAT cycles, a parallel run against the Excel reports for one month close, training sessions for the 4 teams and 3 weeks of hypercare.
out_of_scope: Any application UI or custom web portal.
Real-time or streaming dashboards (the daily batch is enough).
Machine learning models such as demand forecasting or price optimization.
Self-service data preparation training beyond the 4 sessions.
Replacing or changing the source systems (POS, ERP, Shopify, loyalty app).
Power BI licenses and Azure subscription costs (paid by the client).
Cleaning of source data errors inside the source systems.
constraints: Budget ceiling communicated informally: about USD 140k.
Kickoff on 2026-06-01 and go-live by 2026-10-16, about 4.5 months, before the Q4 planning cycle.
Data residency: all data stays in the Azure Brazil South region.
The IT Manager is available about 4 h/week; business stakeholders attend one weekly 1-hour review.
Store networks are connected by VPN to headquarters; the POS databases can only be queried outside trading hours (22:00 to 05:00).
Target scale: about 85,000 tickets per day, 24 months of history (about 1.5 billion ticket lines) and a daily load finished by 06:00.
Loyalty customer data is personal data and must be masked for roles that do not need it.

proposed_stack.ingestion: Azure Data Factory with a self-hosted integration runtime for the store SQL Servers and the Oracle ERP, Python loaders for the Shopify API and the supplier SFTP files.
proposed_stack.lakehouse: Azure Databricks with PySpark and Delta Lake (bronze, silver, gold) on ADLS Gen2, Unity Catalog for governance.
proposed_stack.modeling: dbt Core on Databricks SQL, Great Expectations checks on critical tables.
proposed_stack.bi: Power BI (semantic models, row-level security by store region), Power BI deployment pipelines.
proposed_stack.infra: Terraform, Azure DevOps pipelines, Azure Monitor, Azure Key Vault.

Two review rounds on the dashboards and 2 UAT cycles of 1 week each, executed by the client.
Metric definitions are agreed in 4 workshops; changes after the signed glossary go through change control.

meeting.title: Discovery call — Policy administration system modernization for Seguros Andina

meeting_summary.context_and_problem: Seguros Andina is an insurance broker with 120 employees and about 85,000 active policies. Its policy administration system is a 12-year-old monolith built on .NET Framework 4.6 and Web Forms, backed by a SQL Server database with about 400 tables and 600 stored procedures. Only two developers understand it, there is no automated test suite, and every release needs a full weekend of manual deployment and checking. Last year 3 of 9 releases needed a rollback or an emergency hotfix, and the business has stopped asking for changes because they are too risky. Month-end closing requires the system to be available without interruption.
meeting_summary.goal: Modernize the system incrementally with the strangler pattern, without adding new features. Policy issuance, endorsements and renewals move to .NET 8 services behind an API gateway, and the broker-facing screens move to Angular, in 3 releases. Success criteria stated by the client: zero downtime during month-end closing windows, every release deployed on a weekday evening in under 2 hours, no unexplained differences between old and new in the parallel-run reconciliation reports before each cutover, and at least one client developer able to maintain each migrated module.
in_scope: Reverse engineering of the issuance, endorsement and renewal flows (about 150 stored procedures and 14 Web Forms screens) and a written specification of their business rules.
Characterization tests (xUnit with Verify snapshots) covering about 120 issuance, 80 endorsement and 60 renewal scenarios, plus golden-master tests for premium and tariff calculation.
Playwright UI regression suite for the 14 legacy screens in scope.
YARP API gateway in front of the legacy application, with routing by screen and by broker group and feature flags for gradual cutover.
Synchronization between legacy and new code using SQL Server Change Data Capture on 60 tables, RabbitMQ with MassTransit, and write-back to the legacy tables while old screens still run.

Three .NET 8 services (policy issuance, endorsements, renewals) with ASP.NET Core Web API, Entity Framework Core and MediatR, including premium and tariff calculation and policy certificate PDFs with parity to the legacy output.
Angular 17 application with NgRx and Angular Material replacing 14 screens: policy search and list (2), issuance wizard (5), endorsements (3), renewals (3) and policy detail (1).
Custom reconciliation tool and 3 parallel runs of 4 weeks each, one before each release cutover.
Four environments (dev, test, staging, production) in the client's VMware datacenter, Azure DevOps pipelines, Octopus Deploy and Seq with Serilog.
Three incremental releases with cutover runbooks, rollback plans, 2 weeks of hypercare each, and 3 UAT cycles of 1 week.
Documentation, pairing with the 2 client developers and 6 broker training sessions.
out_of_scope: New features or changes to business rules, including new products and tariffs
Migration of the other modules (accounting, commissions, claims, reporting), which stay on the legacy system
Replacement of SQL Server or any change to the system-of-record database
Cloud migration; everything stays in the client's datacenter
Native mobile apps or a broker self-service portal
Rewrite of the legacy stored procedures that are not part of issuance, endorsements and renewals
Data cleansing of historical policies beyond what the reconciliation reports reveal
Hardware and VMware licensing
constraints: Budget ceiling communicated informally: about USD 190k.
Kickoff on 2026-02-02 and final cutover planned by 2026-10-09 (36 weeks) with a buffer until 2026-10-30, 3 releases about 3 months apart.
Zero downtime in month-end closing windows: no cutover or deployment in the last 5 and first 3 business days of any month.
The two client developers are the only source of legacy knowledge and are available about 8 h/week each for workshops and reviews.
Everything must run in the client's datacenter on VMware; the legacy application and the new services must coexist with no changes to how brokers log in.
Data stays on premises; production snapshots used for tests must be anonymized.
Target scale: about 85,000 active policies, 200 concurrent broker users, month-end peak of about 6,000 issuance and endorsement transactions per day.
Brokers must keep the same screen flow and field order wherever possible, to avoid retraining beyond a short session.

proposed_stack.backend: C# on .NET 8: ASP.NET Core Web API, Entity Framework Core, MediatR; YARP as strangler gateway; RabbitMQ with MassTransit for events between old and new.
proposed_stack.frontend: Angular 17 with NgRx and Angular Material.
proposed_stack.data: SQL Server stays as the system of record; SQL Server Change Data Capture feeds the synchronization layer.
proposed_stack.legacy: .NET Framework 4.6 Web Forms, kept running and wrapped by the gateway during the transition.
proposed_stack.quality: xUnit, Verify (snapshot-based characterization tests), Playwright for UI regression, custom reconciliation tool for parallel runs.
proposed_stack.infra: Client datacenter (VMware), Docker on Linux and Windows VMs, Azure DevOps pipelines, Octopus Deploy, Seq and Serilog.

integrations: Legacy Web Forms application: reached through the YARP gateway and the shared SQL Server database; the client's developers provide a full code and database backup in week 1.
SQL Server 2019 database: CDC is enabled by the client's DBA on the 60 agreed tables after the performance impact is measured in the test environment.
RabbitMQ cluster of 3 nodes on client VMs, provisioned by client IT.
Azure DevOps and Octopus Deploy: existing client tenant and server, with service accounts created by client IT.
Existing broker login (Web Forms authentication): the identity bridge reads the legacy session cookie, with no change for end users.
assumptions: Client IT provisions the 4 VMware environments, RabbitMQ and Octopus within 3 weeks of kickoff.
A restored production snapshot is available in week 2; anonymization is done by us and approved by the client's Head of IT.
Business rules are as the legacy code behaves today; when code and documentation differ, the code wins and the difference is recorded in the specification.
14 screens in scope, with the same fields and flow as today; client feedback within 2 business days and one consolidated round of changes per release.
Each release has one parallel run of 4 weeks with a daily reconciliation report reviewed by the client's Head of Underwriting.
3 UAT cycles of 1 week, one per release, with up to 6 broker users each.
Hypercare is 2 weeks after each cutover; after the last one, support is handled by the client's developers under a separate agreement.
Release 1 covers issuance, release 2 endorsements and release 3 renewals, each with its gateway routes, Angular screens and synchronization.

risks.description: Undocumented business rules hidden in stored procedures and Web Forms code will be discovered late, adding work to the service ports and characterization suites.
Only two people know the legacy system; if either is unavailable or leaves, discovery and parallel-run triage slow down sharply.
The synchronization layer may introduce data drift or contention on the legacy database, especially at month-end peaks, and CDC adds load to a database with 600 stored procedures.
Parallel-run discrepancies may be caused by legacy defects that brokers rely on; deciding whether to reproduce or fix them needs client sign-off and can delay a cutover.
The no-cutover window around month-end leaves limited slots per release; a slipped cutover can push the release by a full month.
Client infrastructure (VMware VMs, RabbitMQ, CDC permissions) may be delivered late, blocking the pipelines and synchronization work.
Broker resistance to new screens may generate late change requests, despite the same-flow, same-fields rule.
